citations.S1: builds SQL by string interpolation from request input
citations.S2: Connection and cursor are never closed — medium.
citations.S3: `"Order #" + order[0]` concatenates a `str` with `order[0]`, which is the SQL `id` column — an integer. This raises `TypeError`
citations.S4: `total / len(orders)` raises `ZeroDivisionError` whenever a user has no orders in that status
citations.S5: Money handled as binary float — medium.
citations.S6: A negative `pct` increases the price; `pct > 100` yields a negative price.
citations.S7: validate `status` against an allowlist of known statuses
citations.S10: `str(order[1])` can render as `19.990000000004` or `20.0` instead of `$20.00`
citations.S11: risking a raw traceback/DB details leaking to the client. Fix: catch `sqlite3.Error`, log it with context, raise a sanitized exception
citations.S12: use `Decimal` (or integer minor units) for all money arithmetic, and round explicitly once at the boundary
citations.S13: The query has no `LIMIT`/pagination, so a user with a very large order history returns everything into memory
citations.S14: Callers index by position (`o[1]`, `order[0]`) with no names; a column reorder in the `SELECT` silently breaks every caller
